extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA) in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kae and Christopher Kanan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection for VQA datasets involves either human annotators generating questions and answers for images, or automated NLP algorithms deriving them from existing image captions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images are primarily sourced from the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO) dataset, NYU-DepthV2 Dataset, Flickr100M, and synthetic cartoon imagery.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA, workers were asked to 'Stump a smart robot' to generate questions, and a separate pool of workers generated answers. For Visual Genome, annotators asked free-form questions and region-specific questions based on bounding boxes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement is analyzed, showing that subjective questions cause disagreement and lack a single objectively correct answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: COCO-VQA consists of three questions per image, with ten answers per question. Visual Genome has an average of 17 QA pairs per image.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA can aid blind and visually impaired individuals by providing information about images on the web and in the real world.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Datasets contain strong language biases where questions can often be answered without the image, and answer distributions are highly skewed (e.g., 'yes' is much more common than 'no').
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include grammatical errors from NLP generation, subjective questions lacking objective answers, and severe language biases that allow algorithms to guess answers without visual reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, evaluating, and benchmarking Visual Question Answering (VQA) algorithms.

name.evidence: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges

description.evidence: In this review, we critically examine the current state of VQA in terms of problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms.

publisher.evidence: Chester F. Carlson Center for Imaging Science Rochester Institute of Technology, Rochester, NY, 14623, USA

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to `Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions. [...] In COCO-QA [31], QA pairs are created for images using an Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithm that derives them from the COCO image captions.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions [...] QA pairs are created for images using an Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithm

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: With exception of DAQUAR, all of the datasets include images from the Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO) dataset [...] Visual Genome and Visual7W use images from Flickr100M in addition to the COCO images. A portion of The VQA Dataset contains synthetic cartoon imagery [...] DAQUAR [...] based on images from the NYU-DepthV2 Dataset

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image by being asked to `Stump a smart robot,' and a separate pool of workers were hired to generate the answers to the questions. [...] prompting workers to ask questions about specific image regions. When using this regionspecific method, a worker might be prompted to ask a question about a region of an image containing a fire hydrant.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers were employed to generate questions for each image

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Using Accuracy V QA, the inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is only 83.3%. It is impossible for an algorithm to achieve 100% accuracy. Inter-human agreement is especially poor for `Why' questions [...] The VQA Dataset contains subjective questions that are prone to cause disagreement between annotators and also clearly lack a single objectively correct answer.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: COCO-VQA consists of three questions per image, with ten answers per question. [...] Visual Genome [...] contains 1.7 million QA pairs for images, with an average of 17 QA pairs per image.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: In COCO-QA [31], QA pairs are created for images using an Natural Language Processing (NLP) algorithm that derives them from the COCO image captions.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: The models also span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The most immediate is as an aid to blind and visually impaired individuals, enabling them to get information about images both on the web and in the real world.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Language bias in datasets critically affects the performance of the current VQA systems [...] `yes/no' answers span about 38% of all questions, and almost 59% of them are answered with `yes.' [...] For COCO-VQA, `yes' is a much more common answer than `no,' simply because people tend to ask questions biased toward `yes' as an answer.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The biggest shortcoming of COCO-QA is due to flaws in the NLP algorithm [...] results in awkwardly phrased questions, with many containing grammatical errors, and others being completely unintelligible [...] COCO-VQA has a large variety of questions, but many of them can be accurately answered without using the image due to language biases.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: These datasets enable VQA systems to be trained and evaluated.
